settings.description: A PEM bundle of certificates trusted, beside the system's, when connecting to the ACME directory: for a private ACME server. Empty trusts the system roots.
The ACME directory of the certificate authority that issues the edge's certificates when Pando orders them itself.
The CPU each new app may use, in thousandths of a CPU. An app can override its own. 0 means 1000, one CPU.
The disk each new app may use, in bytes. An app can override its own. 0 means 10 GiB.
Pull a private image with the Docker login on the Pando server when the app has no registry credential of its own. Off by default: it lends every app on the install whatever that login can read.
The memory each new app may use, in bytes. An app can override its own. 0 means 512 MiB.

The first administrator's password, for an unattended install. Read only on first run, and the account must change it at first sign-in. Empty: the administrator is set up in the console with the setup token Pando prints to its log.
A file holding the first administrator's password, in place of admin_password. An empty file is no password. The bundled Compose file writes PANDO_ADMIN_PASSWORD here.
How long Pando keeps trying to reach Postgres at startup before giving up.
The most connections this replica opens to Postgres. Postgres's max_connections must allow this for every replica, plus a few more for each.
A file holding the password for the database URL's user, which the URL then leaves out. The bundled Compose file generates one on first start.
The Postgres connection string. The bundled Compose file supplies it; set it to use an existing database. Its account must be able to manage Pando's application role.
Write logs as colored, human-readable lines rather than JSON.
The least severe log level written: debug, info, warn or error.
How often metrics are pushed.
The OpenTelemetry collector Pando pushes its own metrics to, such as http://otel-collector:4318 for HTTP or :4317 for gRPC. Empty exports nothing.
Headers sent with every export, as key=value pairs separated by commas with values URL-encoded, as OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS takes them. Usually an API key.
The OTLP protocol: http/protobuf or grpc.

The retry schedule after a failed deploy or restart, as durations separated by commas: the first retry waits the first, and so on. Empty means 0s,5s,15s,60s,5m. Leave it unset in production; Pando warns at startup when it is faster.
How many failures within failure_window before an app is given up on and left failed. 0 means 10.
The window failures are counted in, measured from the last failure. 0 means 30 minutes.
How often garbage collection runs. 0 means an hour.
Send every build through the registry, even when the runtime could import it directly.
Allow plain HTTP to the registry.
How Pando signs in to the registry: basic (a username and password) or ecr (an AWS access key).
How images are arranged in the registry: per_app (a repository per app) or single (one repository for every image). Empty means the kind's default.
The registry password or access token. With kind ecr, the AWS secret access key. Read from the environment only, never from the config file.
A file holding the registry password, in place of password.

The image registry Pando pushes builds to, with an optional path prefix, such as https://registry.internal:5000 or 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/pando. Set, it declares the install's image registry adapter. Empty: no registry, which single-host Docker does not need.
The registry username. With kind ecr, the AWS access key ID.
How long a deleted app's detection and backup records are kept. 0 means 30 days.
How many deployments are kept for each app. 0 means 50.
How long the event outbox is kept. 0 means 30 days.
How long idempotency keys are kept. 0 means a day.
How long security scans are kept. 0 means 90 days.
How long expired or revoked sessions are kept. 0 means 30 days.
How long expired sign-in flows are kept. 0 means a day.
The address the console, the API and the proxy listen on, as host:port. A bare :port listens on every interface.

Where other Pando replicas reach this one, for a deploy's live log. Empty means http://<hostname> and the port of addr, which is right on a Compose network. In Kubernetes, the pod's address, such as http://$(POD_IP):8080.
Where Pando keeps audit log archives itself, when host policy's audit_archive is keep.
The domain per-app subdomains are made under, so an app called notes is reached at notes.example.com. Used only when routing by subdomain.

The address browsers reach Pando on, such as https://pando.example.com. Set it whenever something else terminates TLS: its scheme is what marks session cookies Secure. Empty is right when Pando serves TLS itself, or on plain-HTTP localhost.
The iss claim in every identity assertion Pando sends an app. It names this installation to the apps behind it.
The last host port given to an app when apps are reached by port.
The first host port given to an app when apps are reached by port.
The address routing adapters send app traffic to, which is Pando's own proxy. It must be reachable from wherever the routing adapter runs. Empty means http://pando:8080, the Compose service.
How new apps are addressed by default: path (under Pando's own address), subdomain (each app at its own name under base_domain), or port (each app on its own port).
How long Pando waits for requests in flight to finish when it is stopped.
The file holding the key API tokens are stored under. Made on first start. Every replica must read the same file, and a disaster-recovery bundle carries it.
The proxies in front of Pando whose X-Forwarded-For header names the client in the audit log: addresses and CIDR ranges, separated by commas. Empty records the connecting address.
Where a disaster-recovery bundle is assembled before it is encrypted and sent. It needs room for a database dump and every app volume.
How many apps the leader checks for new commits at once. 0 means eight.
How many rolling backups the leader takes at once. 0 means two.
The older name for host policy's max_concurrent_deploys. Set, it fixes that policy setting unless the policy setting is also set.
How many detections this replica runs at once. 0 means one per CPU, and at least two.
Verbs an agent's token may not use: denied to CLI and MCP tokens only, not to people.
Older form of public_sharing: false means apps cannot be shared with everyone. Prefer public_sharing.
Let apps together ask for more CPU than the runtime has. Off by default: a deploy that would need more CPU than is left is refused. On, busy apps share the CPU and run slower.

Let apps together ask for more memory than the runtime has. Off by default: a deploy that would need more memory than is left is refused. On, the host may run out and stop an app to free memory. Disk is never oversubscribed.

Let event subscription webhooks send to private addresses — the local network, loopback, and link-local addresses such as a cloud metadata service. Off by default, because anyone who can see an app can subscribe to it.
Where a month of the audit log goes once it is past retention: keep (archived under Pando's own directory), export (to a backup destination), or off (nothing is archived, so nothing is removed).
The backup destination, by adapter ID, that audit archives are exported to when audit_archive is export. Empty means the default backup destination.
How many months the audit log keeps before an older month is archived and removed from the live log. 0 means 3, which is also the least it may be.
Upgrade to new patch releases automatically inside maintenance_window. Takes a database copy for rollback but not a full backup. Needs upgrade_in_place.
Apps, by ID, whose deploys need approval whatever their owners say.
How many approvals a deploy needs. 0 means one.
How long a deploy waits for approval before it expires, in hours. 0 means it waits until somebody answers.
Every app's deploys need approval from somebody holding install.deploys.approve or app.deploy.approve. Automatic deploys stop while it is on.
Turn off AI screening of deployment plans: AI is never sent a repository to repair a plan or answer detection's questions.

Don't record refusals of people who aren't signed in: authz.denied is written for an anonymous visitor to an app not shared with them only while this is off. Refusals of signed-in people and tokens are always recorded.
Don't record visits from people who aren't signed in: app.use is written to the audit log for signed-in people and tokens only, not for anonymous visitors to public apps.
Don't make an account when someone first signs in through an identity provider, whatever the provider is set to. People need an account from SCIM or an administrator first.
Turn off sign-in with a local username and password, so people sign in through an external identity provider. Needs at least one provider turned on.
Don't check GitHub for newer Pando releases. Off sends no request at all, for an installation that has no internet access or may not call out.
Permissions nobody may use, install-wide, including an app's owner. app.exec here is the Policy screen's "Turn off terminal access for the whole installation".
Older form of egress_mode allowlist with egress_list. Prefer those.
Stop apps connecting to private addresses — the local network, loopback, and the cloud metadata address — whatever egress_mode says.
The installation's egress list: hostnames, *.wildcards, addresses or ranges, each optionally with a port. Read by egress_mode.

Whether an app may loosen the installation's egress rules (add to an allowlist, remove from a denylist, unblock private addresses): verb (somebody holding app.egress.loosen may), approval (its deploy needs approval), or forbidden.
Where apps may connect out to: allow_all (anywhere), denylist (anywhere except egress_list), or allowlist (only egress_list). Apps can narrow it; loosening it is governed by egress_loosening.

Delete an app nobody has used for this many days, counted from its last use, so it is longer than idle_stop_days. Its owner is told 7 days before. Storage is backed up first when require_backup_before_destroy is on, and discarded otherwise. An app can set its own number or turn this off. 0 means never.
Stop an app nobody has used for this many days. Its owner is told 7 days before, and somebody starts it again by hand. An app can set its own number or turn this off. 0 means never.
Ignore findings with no fix available, in both the security score and the list.
What happens to a running app that falls below the minimum security score: warn, or stop (after the grace period).
Grace period, in hours, before stop applies to an app below the minimum score.
When automatic upgrades may start, in UTC: weekdays, a start time and a length, such as "sun,wed 02:00 2h" or "daily 03:30 1h".
How many apps each person may own, unless their account or one of their groups says otherwise. 0 means unlimited.
How many deploys each replica of Pando runs at once. A deploy past the limit waits in the queue and its log says how many are ahead of it. 0 means one per CPU, and at least two.
Total disk for app logs across every app, in bytes. 0 means no limit.
Longest a token may live, in days. 0 means no limit.
Minimum isolation for builds, as an isolation class number (10 is a container).
Minimum isolation for running apps, as an isolation class number (10 is a container).
Minimum security score a deploy must reach, 0 to 100. 0 means off.
Whether an app may be shared with anyone on the internet: allowed, passcode_only (only behind the app's passcode), or none.
Require a backup before anything is destroyed: an app's storage is backed up before the app or its volumes are deleted.

Require two-factor authentication on every local account. Someone without it sets it up at their next sign-in, and can do nothing else until they have. Accounts from an identity provider are not affected.

Where apps may be created from: a host (github.com), a host suffix (.corp.example), or a host and path (github.com/acme, ghcr.io/acme) — repositories and image registries alike. Add `upload` to allow files sent from a computer. Empty means anywhere.
Which Pando releases the update check offers: stable (releases only) or prerelease (release candidates too).
Let Pando upgrade itself to a newer release from the Updates screen. Needs Pando's image set to a moving tag such as trypando/pando:latest; usually set in the deployment's configuration.
